title: Harrowmoor Logistics onboarding kickoff
scratchpad:
Harrowmoor = NEW customer, kickoff
35 seats, 1 yr
dispatcher training wk of Oct 19 @ river depot
techs live Mon Nov 2
Wilf = admin, Petra = contracts
segments: Welcome, Petra and Wilf. This is the onboarding kickoff, so the goal is a schedule everyone believes in. Maya from our product team is joining too.
Thanks. We're excited, honestly. We've been running dispatch off three spreadsheets and a whiteboard for far too long.
Quick recap of what you signed: a one year agreement for thirty five technician seats.
That's right. Thirty five covers both depots, with a few spare for the busy season.
Tell us about the depots. How does work flow between them today?
We run two, the river depot and the airport depot. It's mostly appliance deliveries and installs, so washing machines, ovens, and the occasional heat pump.
Each depot has its own dispatcher. They phone each other when one is short of people, which works fine until both of them are on another call.
The double booking is the thing I want gone. Last week we sent one technician to two installs at the same time, on opposite sides of town.
Shared crews across depots are exactly what the dispatch board is built for. One board for both depots, and a technician can only be in one place at a time.
Let's do the schedule. Wilf, you'll be the admin on your side?
Yes, I'll be the admin. Petra signs things, I make them work.
The first step is data. Customer addresses, your regular install locations, and your technician list with their skills.
The addresses are in three spreadsheets that don't agree with each other. I'll need a day just to clean them up.
I'll send the import template by Friday. It has a column for every field, and it flags duplicates when you upload it.
On skills, the scheduler can match jobs to people. If only some technicians can install heat pumps, tag them, and the board won't offer the wrong person.
That would save us a lot of awkward phone calls. Only four of our people are certified for heat pumps.
Next is training. We do the dispatchers first, then the technicians.
Dispatcher training is two sessions in the week of the nineteenth of October, at the river depot, so both dispatchers are in the same room.
That week works. The airport dispatcher can drive over for both sessions.
And when do the technicians go live?
Technicians go live on Monday the second of November. We'd like a week of the dispatchers using the board on their own before the phones start buzzing.
The second of November is fine. It's after our autumn promotion ends, so the volume will be lower that week.
For go-live day, I'd suggest one of our people on site at the river depot. Things always come up that nobody thought of.
I can be there that morning, and at the airport depot in the afternoon.
What do the technicians need? Do they all need new phones?
No, the app runs on the phones they already have. Android or iPhone, as long as it's from the last four or five years.
Good, because a phone budget was definitely not in my plan.
One more thing. Today our office calls each customer when the technician is on the way. Should we keep doing that?
For now, yes. Keep the calls going while everyone gets used to the board, and we'll look at it again once you're settled.
To recap: I send the import template by Friday, Wilf cleans the addresses, dispatcher training is the week of the nineteenth, and technicians go live on the second of November.
And I tag the heat pump people before the import, so the skills are there from day one.
And anything contractual, or anything that needs a signature, comes to me, not to Wilf.
Got it. Thanks, both of you. We're looking forward to this.

items.text: Harrowmoor Logistics signed a one-year agreement for 35 technician seats
Send Harrowmoor the import template by Friday
Dispatcher training: two sessions the week of October 19 at the river depot
Harrowmoor technicians go live on Monday, November 2
